name: Send a Slack safety check when an earthquake hits near your sites, using the USGS feed and Google Sheets

nodes.name: Run once: set up the sheet
Add the Sites and Alerts tabs

parameters.content:
## 1. Every 5 minutes
Config holds the feed, the default magnitude and radius, the language and the time zone.

## 2. Sites, earthquakes, sent alerts
Your sites from the sheet, the USGS real-time feed, and the pairs already sent.

## 3. Code decides
Straight-line distance from the epicentre and the magnitude, per site. Bad coordinates stop the run with a message.

## 4. Ask and remember
One Slack message per earthquake. The pair is stored after the message, so a failed post is tried again.

## Run once: set up the sheet
Paste your spreadsheet ID and run once: it adds the Sites and Alerts tabs with their header rows.

## Earthquake near a site? Ask who is safe, at once
Every 5 minutes the workflow reads the free USGS real-time earthquake feed (no key). For every site in your `Sites` tab (name, latitude, longitude, contact), **code computes the distance from the epicentre** and posts a safety-check message in Slack when the magnitude is at or above your limit and the site is within your radius. The contact is mentioned; people reply in the thread. **No AI is used.**

### How it works
1. Read the Sites tab and the USGS feed (default: M4.5+ of the past hour).
2. Code checks each earthquake against each site (distance and magnitude, per-site limits optional). A wrong coordinate stops the run with a clear message instead of dropping the site.
3. One Slack message per earthquake lists the sites nearby, closest first.
4. The `Alerts` tab stores earthquake + site, so the same pair is never sent twice.

### Setup
1. Blank Google Sheet: paste its ID in **Spreadsheet ID**, run **Run once**, select the sheet in the Google Sheets nodes.
2. Fill the Sites tab: site, lat, lon (right-click the place in Google Maps to copy them), contact (a Slack member ID mentions them).
3. Pick a Slack channel. Set the limits, language and time zone in **Config**. Publish.

### Note
Magnitude is not local shaking intensity. Use it as a trigger to ask, not as a damage report.
